question: What is the primary role of a nurse during community mobilisation?
explanation: The nurse guides and supports the community to take charge of their health rather than dictating solutions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is respecting local culture important in community mobilisation?

options.A: It speeds up the disbursement of government funds
options.B: It allows nurses to bypass traditional rulers
options.C: It prevents the need for any health education
options.D: It builds trust and encourages active participation

explanation: Cultural respect creates a welcoming environment where community members feel valued and willing to engage. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h1)

question: Who must be contacted first when entering a community for health mobilisation?
explanation: Contacting traditional rulers and local leaders ensures cultural entry protocols are properly respected. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h2)

question: A nurse arrives in a new rural posting. What action should be taken first?

options.B: Distribute mosquito nets in the market
options.D: Pay courtesy visits to local leaders

explanation: Official entry requires respecting local hierarchy before rolling out any health activities. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h2)

question: Which communication channel is traditionally effective for rural community sensitization in Nigeria?
explanation: Town criers remain a trusted and direct way to reach every household in many traditional Nigerian settings. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the sensitization step?

options.A: To build awareness and reduce resistance to health programs
options.B: To elect new political leaders for the local government
options.C: To collect taxes for building primary health clinics
options.D: To conduct clinical diagnoses on sick community members

explanation: Sensitization prepares the minds of the people so they accept and participate in subsequent health interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why are local stakeholders trained during community mobilisation?

options.A: To handle political campaigns for the district
options.B: To construct large modern hospitals alone
options.C: To replace professional nurses in the clinics
options.D: To act as sustainable local health champions

explanation: Training locals ensures that health promotion continues long after external health workers leave. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which group is typically included as key stakeholders in rural health mobilisation?

options.C: Federal legislators and high court judges
options.D: Traditional birth attendants and youth leaders

explanation: Local figures like birth attendants and youth leaders hold direct influence over community health behaviors. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h4)

question: What tool is commonly used during participatory needs assessment?
explanation: Focus group discussions allow community members to express their opinions and priorities openly. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why is priority setting necessary after identifying community needs?

options.A: Health workers are legally barred from solving more than one issue
options.B: Communities refuse to discuss more than a single topic
options.C: Resources are limited, so attention must go to the most urgent problem
options.D: Government policy requires exact uniformity across all states

explanation: Prioritizing ensures that scarce resources are channeled toward the most critical health issues first. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the main danger of relying solely on external funding for community projects?

options.A: It eliminates the need for community leaders
options.B: It creates dependency and threatens project sustainability
options.C: It makes the project complete much faster

explanation: When external funds run out, projects often collapse if the community has not contributed local resources. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h6)

question: What does an action plan primarily specify?

options.A: The exact medical diagnosis of every sick person
options.B: The salary scale for incoming foreign doctors
options.C: Who does what, when, and with what resources
options.D: The penal code for health law breakers

explanation: An action plan assigns clear responsibilities and timelines to keep the mobilization process organized. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which activity is an example of implementing a community health intervention?

options.D: Writing a project proposal for donors

explanation: Immunization drives represent direct clinical and public health service delivery to the community. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h7)

question: How do trained community volunteers assist during project implementation?

options.A: By bridging communication gaps and mobilizing residents
options.B: By managing the national health insurance budget
options.C: By prescribing advanced prescription drugs independently
options.D: By performing major surgical procedures in clinics

explanation: Volunteers help gather neighbors, translate instructions, and encourage high turnout for interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation in community health?

options.A: Monitoring is done by villagers, evaluation by politicians
options.B: Monitoring costs money, evaluation is always free
options.C: Monitoring happens at the end, evaluation happens daily
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing, while evaluation assesses overall impact

explanation: Continuous tracking defines monitoring, whereas measuring final outcomes defines evaluation. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h8)

question: What indicates that a community health program has achieved sustainability?

options.A: The government takes over every single task from the locals
options.B: All health workers are permanently redeployed to urban cities
options.C: The community successfully manages and continues activities on its own
options.D: Foreign donors promise to fund the project for twenty more years

explanation: True sustainability means local ownership and self-reliance persist after external support ends. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h8)
